entries.notes: Implemented (#1444): the explicit user Stop. Cancels the generation through the session's shared cancellation token, finalizes and evicts the buffer, and answers an idempotent 204 whether or not the session existed; a missing conv_id is upstream's 400. The recorded cross-key divergence (another key's DELETE is the same 204 but deliberately does not touch the session) is permanent by_design, pinned by stream_sessions_are_isolated_between_api_keys.
divergence: With more than one --api-key configured, sessions are scoped to the key that created them: another key's GET answers the same 404 as an unknown id, its lookup omits the session, and its DELETE is a 204 no-op; b10621 lets any configured key read, discover, and delete any session. With zero or one key the behavior is identical.

rationale.reason: Cross-key session isolation is a security decision: with several --api-key values configured, the holder of one key must not read, discover, or delete sessions another key created, where b10621 treats every configured key as one principal. The refusals are indistinguishable from an unknown id, so no endpoint is an existence oracle across keys.
rationale.revisit_if: the project decides that all configured API keys form a single trust domain, as in b10621, for example behind an explicit opt-in flag that restores upstream's shared session visibility.

entries.notes: Implemented (#1444): replays the exact SSE bytes a streaming completion buffered under its X-Conversation-Id, from the byte offset in `from`, then follows live output until the session finalizes. All five streaming surfaces record sessions (chat completions on both spellings, /v1/completions, native /completion(s), /v1/responses, /v1/messages); the disaggregated router front does not. Buffer cap 4 MiB with front-drop, 300 s post-completion TTL, 60 s GC, plus an mlxcel-side cap of 256 retained completed sessions. Status codes and wording follow upstream server-stream.cpp: 400 'Missing conversation id in path', 404 'Stream not found or expired', 400 'Invalid 'from' offset', 400 'Stream offset lost, please restart'. A client disconnect no longer cancels a session-carrying generation; DELETE and session replacement do, through the same scheduler cancellation token. The recorded cross-key divergence is the authorization ownership #1444 deliberately requires, permanent by_design and pinned by stream_sessions_are_isolated_between_api_keys.
divergence: With more than one --api-key configured, sessions are scoped to the key that created them: another key's GET answers the same 404 as an unknown id, its lookup omits the session, and its DELETE is a 204 no-op; b10621 lets any configured key read, discover, and delete any session. With zero or one key the behavior is identical.

entries.notes: Implemented (#1444): body {id, action}; missing id is 400 'missing completion id', any action other than reasoning_end is 400 'unknown control action', an unknown id is 200 {success:false, message:'no active completion for this id'}, a live completion that did not arm reasoning_control is 200 {success:false, message:'reasoning control not enabled for this completion'}, and an armed one is 200 {success:true}. The force flag is polled by the scheduler's thinking tracker at every sampling step, so the event-order boundary is the next sampled token: committed events are unaffected and the reasoning block closes exactly as an exhausted budget closes it. Streaming chat completions and OpenAI completions register their chatcmpl-/cmpl- ids; the native route arms the tracker but, as in b10621, never reveals an id a control request could target. The recorded cross-key divergence is permanent by_design; the ownership scoping is pinned by cross_owner_control_is_indistinguishable_from_unknown.
divergence: With more than one --api-key configured, a control request presenting a different key than the completion's creator answers {success:false, message:'no active completion for this id'}; b10621 lets any configured key control any live completion. With zero or one key the behavior is identical.

rationale.reason: Cross-key completion-control isolation is a security decision: with several --api-key values configured, the holder of one key must not force reasoning_end on a completion another key created, where b10621 lets any configured key control any live completion. The refusal is indistinguishable from an unknown id, so the endpoint is not an existence oracle across keys.
rationale.revisit_if: the project decides that all configured API keys form a single trust domain, as in b10621, for example behind an explicit opt-in flag that restores upstream's shared control surface.

entries.notes: Implemented (#1444): answers one {conversation_id, is_done, total_bytes, started_at, completed_at} object per matching session, matching each requested id exactly and any '<id>::<model>' per-model variant, and only for ids the caller asked about, so live sessions cannot be enumerated. A malformed body is upstream's 400 'invalid body: ...'. entries.description: Create the budget sampler on demand so reasoning can be ended at runtime
entries.notes: Accepted as a bool (default false) on the chat, OpenAI-completions and native completion requests, upstream's declared schema. Arming creates the runtime force-end flag on the sequence's thinking tracker, upstream's 'create the budget sampler on demand', so POST /v1/chat/completions/control can end the reasoning phase mid-generation; unarmed requests pay nothing.
